Экран настроек Muse теперь ставит коннектор, ведёт вход через Chrome и копирует аккаунт на все машины.

Изменены `app.tsx`, `app.css`, `i18n.ts`.

- Карточка машины: runtime (версия / Installing… / Install / неподдерживаемая ОС) и Chrome; **Install** вызывает `rpc.call("installRuntime")`.
- Пока идёт `addAccount`, на карточке спиннер и текст «A Chrome window opened on …». После успеха — подпись аккаунта и число из `synced` (ошибки синхронизации — по именам машин).
- Если `chromeFound === false`, блок Add заменён текстом со списком подключённых машин с Chrome.
- У аккаунта кнопки Check, **Copy to all machines** (`syncAccounts`) и Remove.

Проверки: `node /tmp/muse-settings-check/check.mjs` → OK; `node --test tests/i18n.test.mjs tests/ui-style.test.mjs` → 3 pass; `npm run typecheck` → 0.

В `accountRow` нет `busy`/`max`, поэтому слоты на строке не рисуются — в RPC их нет, `server.ts` вне scope.

```plan-fact
]
```

APPROACH: UI читает уже существующие RPC `installRuntime`, `syncAccounts` и поле `synced` у `addAccount`; строки только через i18n, цвета через `--pk-*`.
LESSON: Слоты busy/max в статусе аккаунта не приходят — для строки таблицы их нельзя нарисовать, пока host RPC не отдаст поля.

dispatchContext.rulesText:
- In verification scripts and tests that create temp dirs, use /tmp explicitly (mktemp -d /tmp/x.XXXXXX, or TMPDIR=/tmp): the writer sandbox denies mkdtemp in the system TMPDIR under /var/folders. Keep PM-written check scripts in /tmp/<name>/ (the guard blocks .mjs under .agents/).
- In a folder without git (live-folder mode), never put a task's expected_outputs or owns_paths under .bb/ (chat folders): the live snapshot skips .bb, so a file written there is never counted as produced and the task blocks as missing expected_outputs. Put task deliverables in a project folder such as docs/ or reports/.
- Generate site designs without waiting for the owner's approval; keep iterating and testing until the result is a genuinely modern, colorful, attractive site, not a bland one.
- When generating a site screen by screen, pass the previous screen to the generator and tell it which next screen of the same site it is producing, so the screens read as one coherent site.

{"summary":"This bounded context summarizes the excerpts provided for task muse-settings-v2 (lane muse-ui) within the muse-ai-connector plugin. The objective of this task is to deliver a complete, polished Settings screen in BB (Settings → Plugins → Muse) that allows users to manage Muse accounts, observe runtime status across all connected BB machines, trigger runtime installation, execute an intuitive sign-in flow that opens Chrome on an appropriate host, and synchronize account credentials across all connected machines including headless environments.

Architectural Context & Packaging Plan (.agents/plans/muse-packaging.md):
The packaging plan addresses zero-terminal onboarding for BB users. BB hosts receive only bundled host.mjs artifacts; CLI binaries (bin/, bridge/) and node_modules are not distributed via the host bundle. To make Muse operational, the packaging plan establishes four pieces: Piece A (runtime self-install into ~/.muse-bridge/runtime/<version>/ with bin shims), Piece B (hub-coordinated account export/import across hosts), Piece C (Settings screen UI, which is the current task), and Piece D (comprehensive documentation). The settings UI task depends on upstream contracts from muse-runtime-install (exposing runtime status and installRuntime RPC) and muse-hub-sync (exposing syncAccounts RPC and syncing logic upon account creation).

Current Settings Implementation in app.tsx:
The existing app.tsx defines a settings section 'muse-accounts' using @get-bb/plugin-sdk/app. It displays connected hosts (HostCard) and their accounts (AccountCard), but reflects an earlier, incomplete version of the feature set:
1. Runtime Status & Actions: HostCard displays rows for Google Chrome (chromeFound/chromePath), Bridge (bridgeFound/bridgeVersion), and Agent (agentFound). It lacks a unified runtime line indicating whether the runtime is installed, currently installing, unsupported, or missing, as well as the 'Install' button calling rpc.call('installRuntime').
2. Account Actions: AccountCard currently displays account labels, status pills (busy, signed_in, signed_out, unknown), last used timestamps, and actions for checking status or removing accounts (with a profile purge option). It lacks the 'Copy to all machines' button which must invoke rpc.call('syncAccounts', { id }).
3. Sign-in Flow & In-Flight State: When adding an account, HostCard simply presents a text input and 'Add account' button that directly triggers rpc.call('addAccount', { hostId, label }). It does not implement the required in-progress state notifying the user that a Chrome window has opened on the specified machine with a spinner and cancel hint, nor does it display the post-sign-in success state reporting the account label and the number of synchronized machines.
4. Headless & Chrome-less Machines: The Add account form is currently rendered regardless of whether Google Chrome is detected on the host. Under the new requirements, if st.chromeFound is false, the Add account input and button must be hidden and replaced with informative i18n text identifying connected machines that do possess Chrome where the account should be added instead.

Localization Invariants in i18n.ts:
The plugin mandates bilingual support (English default, Russian when document.documentElement.lang starts with 'ru'). The ru dictionary is strictly typed as Record<I18nKey, string>, requiring exact key parity with en. Currently, i18n.ts contains 31 keys covering basic statuses, errors, and removal confirmations. It lacks translation keys for the new runtime status states (installed, installing, install button, unsupported), account copying/syncing, in-flight Chrome sign-in guidance, success messaging with machine counts, and fallback guidance for Chrome-less hosts.

Styling Invariants in app.css:
All styling adheres to the Pokecut design language. The CSS maps --pk-* tokens to local --muse-* variables with fallbacks to standard BB theme variables (--card, --border, --muted, --primary, --destructive, etc.). Component classes include panels, cards, rows, action bars, inputs, buttons, and status pills. No raw hex or rgb color literals exist. To fulfill the task acceptance criteria, app.css may need to define spinner styles or layout adjustments for the in-flight sign-in panel and sync feedback messages while strictly preserving Pokecut token constraints.

Backend & RPC Interface Observations (server.ts):
The excerpt of server.ts defines rpcContract with methods hosts, addAccount, checkAccounts, and removeAccount. Notably, in the provided excerpt, rpcContract does not yet declare syncAccounts or installRuntime, and hostStatus does not yet include a runtime property. Because server.ts and host.ts are explicitly out of scope and listed under never_touch, the UI implementation in app.tsx must be written against the expected signatures established by the prerequisite tasks (muse-runtime-install and muse-hub-sync).

Verification & Acceptance:
Acceptance requires that: (a) while addAccount runs, an in-progress state shows that Chrome opened on that machine with a spinner, followed by success text reporting the account label and synced machine count; (b) machines with chromeFound === false hide the Add block and display i18n text naming connected Chrome-equipped machines; (c) each account row offers Check, Copy to all machines, and
